parts.text:
I'm manually working through the plant dataset—8 plants across 5 timepoints, split between control (P01-P04) and drought (P05-P08) groups. P04's day-6 height reading of 119.5 stands out as an obvious data error, probably meant to be 11.95, and the subsequent values back to normal range support that suspicion.

Using height gain (day 12 minus day 0) as the growth metric, control plants average 12.82 cm of growth versus 7.55 cm for drought plants, a difference of 5.27 cm, meaning drought plants gained only about 59% as much. Since this metric relies only on endpoints, the P04 outlier at day 6 doesn't distort these gain calculations, though it would matter if I used slope-based regression across all timepoints instead. I'm now computing standard deviations for each group to assess the spread, starting with the control group's gains and getting a standard deviation around 0.64.

I continue this with the drought group, getting a standard deviation near 0.27, then run a Welch's t-test by hand — standard error around 0.348, t-statistic roughly 15, and Welch-Satterthwaite degrees of freedom around 4, suggesting a p-value well under 0.001, though I note this is a rough hand calculation rather than something verified with a statistical tool. I also check the starting heights: drought plants actually began slightly taller on average (4.99 cm vs. 4.80 cm for control), which if anything makes the final gain difference more conservative, and I'm now comparing the final day-12 heights between groups to confirm the pattern holds.

I spot a clear data quality issue: plant P04's day-6 height of 119.5 cm is almost certainly a decimal-point error (likely meant to be 11.95 cm), since it breaks an otherwise smooth growth trajectory — this wouldn't affect endpoint-only comparisons but would badly skew any slope or AUC-based analysis. I also note leaf-count trajectories look consistent, review that there's no information on replicate trays or randomization (making it hard to separate treatment effects from pot/bench placement), and confirm growth looks essentially linear across the five measured days aside from that one outlier, which happens to fall in the control group.

So the final answer: drought plants gained noticeably less height (mean gain ~7.55 cm vs ~12.82 cm for control, about 41% less growth) and fewer new leaves (3 vs an average of 4.25 in control). I want to flag that I calculated this by hand rather than scripting it, estimate a rough Welch's t-test suggesting p well below 0.001, and recommend verifying the suspicious P04 value against raw records plus offering to script the analysis for reproducibility. A small table of per-plant gains would help present this clearly.

**Yes, the drought plants grew less.** Over the 12 days, drought plants gained about 5.3 cm less height than controls and added fewer leaves.

| Plant | Treatment | Height day 0 (cm) | Height day 12 (cm) | Height gain (cm) | Leaves day 0 → 12 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| P01 | control | 4.86 | 17.48 | 12.62 | 3 → 7 |
| P02 | control | 4.89 | 17.14 | 12.25 | 3 → 7 |
| P03 | control | 4.66 | 17.33 | 12.67 | 3 → 7 |
| P04 | control | 4.78 | 18.52 | 13.74 | 3 → 8 |
| P05 | drought | 5.38 | 12.79 | 7.41 | 3 → 6 |
| P06 | drought | 4.69 | 12.43 | 7.74 | 3 → 6 |
| P07 | drought | 5.11 | 12.35 | 7.24 | 3 → 6 |
| P08 | drought | 4.76 | 12.57 | 7.81 | 3 → 6 |

**Summary numbers (hand-calculated from the table above):**
- Mean height gain: control 12.82 cm (SD 0.64), drought 7.55 cm (SD 0.27). The difference is 5.27 cm, so drought plants gained about 59% of the control gain.
- Mean final height: control 17.62 cm, drought 12.54 cm.
- Mean leaves added: control 4.25, drought 3.0.
- Welch t-test on height gain: t ≈ 15, df ≈ 4, p well below 0.001 (approximate).

The drought group also started slightly taller on average (4.99 cm vs 4.80 cm), so the gap is not caused by a smaller starting size.

**Data problems to check:**
1. **P04, day 6: height 119.5 cm.** The neighbouring values are 8.2 cm (day 3) and 15.32 cm (day 9), so this is almost certainly a typo, possibly 11.95. It doesn't affect the day 0 → day 12 gain, but it would distort any trajectory, slope or area-under-curve analysis. Check the original notes before using the trajectory data.
2. **Small sample.** There are only four plants per treatment, and the file doesn't say whether plants were randomized or whether they shared a bench, tray or watering line. Any location effect would be confounded with treatment.
3. **Unclear units and metadata.** The file has no column notes, plant-to-pot mapping, or measurement method for leaf count, so I can't rule out differences in how they were recorded.

The day-12 comparison holds regardless of the P04 error. If you want a trajectory analysis, fix or exclude that value first. I can also write a script so the analysis is reproducible. The source is `/home/user/clio-cloudlive-ws/greenhouse_trial.csv`.
